title: Add landing reconcile step run at start of land and status
summary: Add a reconcile step (§8.1, D111) in athena-core. It finds main's first-parent commits since the last landing record that have no landing record. It matches each to a landing-intent by head tree and expected base (parent) and writes the missing landing record. With no match it asks the host which PR merged. If the host can't answer, it reports the commit as unattributed and writes nothing. It runs at the start of `athena land` and `athena status`. The audience is the maintainer and the verifier, who check the crash-repair, host-unavailable and no-intent cases.

defaults_applied.how: All new code and tests are Rust.
New module has unit tests for the three named cases; cargo test and clippy are clean.
The criteria run the three named crash/host scenarios rather than checking that types exist.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
One focused change: reconcile plus its two call sites.
Reuse the existing gh.rs and records helpers; no new crate.
Doc comments cite §8.1 and D111, and the CHANGELOG entry is written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The reconcile logic lives in athena-core, behind traits for the host and the records sink so tests can fake them. This follows the existing LandingRecords/Runner pattern in gh.rs.
'Last landing record' is the checkpoint: only first-parent commits after the newest commit that has a landing record are examined. Older commits are not re-examined.
A match means the intent's head tree equals the commit's tree and the intent's expected base equals the commit's first parent. The commit sha written to the landing record is the main commit's.
A commit with no intent and no host answer is reported (not an error exit by itself) and nothing is written. A human declaring it as an intervention is out of scope.
The repository lacks the 'inside the check' part (athena check --history), which this job does not wire in. Only land and status are in scope.
A failure to reach the host is treated the same as 'host cannot answer'.

acceptance_criteria.text: Crash repair: a test creates a main commit whose tree and parent match a landing-intent, with no landing record. Reconcile writes the landing record with the host-made commit sha, using only the intent and without calling the host. Check with `cargo test`.
Host unavailable: a test with a main commit that has no matching intent and a host that errors returns an 'unattributed' finding for that commit and writes no landing record. Check with `cargo test`.

No guessing: a test with a commit that has no intent and no merged pull request reports the commit as unattributed and writes nothing. It never attributes the commit to a nearby intent or PR. Check with `cargo test`.

A host fallback test: when no intent matches and the host names the merged PR, the landing record is written for that PR. A commit that already has a landing record, or that predates the last landing record, is skipped. Check with `cargo test`.

`athena land` and `athena status` call reconcile before their other work. A test or CLI test shows an unattributed commit surfaced in their output. Check with `cargo test`; `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the reconcile step that cites docs/design/records-history.md §8.1 and D111, job 3 part 2.

Per the buy-first default, the change reuses the existing host and git helpers (GitLandingRecords, RecordsWriter, the history record types) and adds no new dependency. No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) changes.

out_of_scope: Running reconcile inside `athena check --history` or at the start of every other command.
Declaring unattributed commits as interventions (§8.1 step 4).
Changes to the records-branch writer's compare-and-swap or retry logic (§8.2).
Any change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or CI workflows.
departures: The cost and time figures are above the reference. The work spans the core, git and cli crates, and the tests need fake git history, intents and host.
